correctness.rationale: The centered finite-variance two-flip skeleton is spatially oscillatory, ensuring all levels are hit. The bounded two-state backward hitting ODE has unique bounded solution with exponential root sqrt(v^2+2Df)/D. Strong Markov at successive level hits yields a spatial chain with rates a_D=(sqrt(v^2+2Df)-v)/(2D), b_D=(sqrt(v^2+2Df)+v)/(2D). Coupling independent exponential run lengths with fixed unit exponentials gives a_D->f/(2v), (v/D)/b_D->1, local tightness and the marked Poisson limit; finite-grid hitting computation errors <1e-5.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the explicit small-D marked Poisson law of wrong-polarity first-visit paint islands, not the previously known Markov-modulated Brownian ladder property. Full source text of arXiv:2603.24277v1 reports one-point paint probabilities and integrated coverage, only qualitative island sizes. The main strong-cover risk is that general first-passage matrix equations plus standard rare-state renewal point-process theory imply the result, though no directly stated equivalent theorem was identified.
residual_risks: A general Markov-modulated Brownian ladder-phase theorem already implies spatial Markovianity; that is treated as prior, not as new.
The explicit marked-Poisson limit might be recoverable as a corollary of a general rare-fast-state theorem not identified in the literature search.
The complete text of the 2026 first-passage book chapter and the 2017 journal article was not inspected; their abstracts establish generic covering structures but not the exact painted-island limit.

value.rationale: The motivating source explicitly identifies rare opposite-polarity paint islands as an essential physical microstructure but supplies only their qualitative scale. Exact Poisson island counts and independent scaled exponential widths describe a natural directly interpretable spatial observable even though the total minority fraction vanishes; they are not mere reparameterizations of the known one-point fractions.
